Rock of Ages
rŏk ŭv āj´ĕz
n. phrase (a title of God drawn from the margin of Isaiah 26:4; the everlasting Rock in whom His people trust)
The AV text of Isaiah 26:4 reads “everlasting strength”; the marginal reading is the rock of ages, rendering the Hebrew tsur olamim. Toplady's hymn of 1763 took its title from that margin, and the phrase has been sung ever since by people who never read the note.

Biblical Definition

The Rock of Ages is God as the unchanging refuge. Isaiah's charge is: “Trust ye in the LORD for ever: for in the LORD JEHOVAH is everlasting strength” (Isa 26:4) — where the margin reads, the rock of ages. The title is Moses' first: “He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he” (Deu 32:4). David piles it up: “The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my strength, in whom I will trust” (Psa 18:2). Paul identifies it: the fathers “drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ” (1Co 10:4). And the Lord makes it the test of a life's foundation (Mat 7:24–25).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines rock as a large mass of stony matter, and, in Scripture, figuratively, defense, protection, refuge — and notes that God is called a rock, as the refuge and defense of his people.

expand to see more

ROCK, n. A large mass of stony matter, usually compounded of two or more simple minerals, either bedded in the earth or resting on its surface.

2. In Scripture, figuratively, defense; means of safety; protection; strength; asylum.

The Lord is my rock. 2 Sam. 22.

3. Firmness; a firm or immoveable foundation.

4. A species of vulture or condor.

Key Scripture

Isa 26:4 — "Trust ye in the LORD for ever: for in the LORD JEHOVAH is everlasting strength:"

Deu 32:4 — "He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he."

Psa 18:2 — "The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my strength, in whom I will trust; my buckler, and the horn of my salvation, and my high tower."

1Co 10:4 — "And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ."

Mat 7:24 — "Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:"

Modern Corruption

The figure is heard as sentiment, and in Scripture a rock is chosen for one property: it does not move when everything else does.

expand to see more

The metaphor is not decorative and it is not about grandeur. In the terrain the psalms come out of, a rock is where a hunted man goes — a cleft, a crag, a height an enemy cannot easily reach — and David wrote most of these lines while being pursued through exactly that country. Webster catches it: in Scripture, figuratively, defense; means of safety; protection; asylum. When a psalm calls God a rock it is making a claim about survivability under attack, by a man who had tested the ordinary kind.

Deuteronomy 32:4 is the fullest statement and it defines the rock by moral rather than physical properties: his work is perfect, for all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he. That is what makes Him a place to stand. A refuge that were merely powerful would be no refuge at all if it were arbitrary, and the whole comfort of the figure depends on the character clauses. Moses sings this in a song God told him to teach Israel against the day they would forget it.

First Corinthians 10:4 makes the identification explicit and the church has sung it ever since: that Rock was Christ. Paul is reading the wilderness narrative — the rock struck at Horeb, the water that followed a nation through forty years of desert — and saying the supply was a Person. Which is also why Toplady's hymn asks the Rock to be cleft for me, since the rock in Exodus gave water only after it was struck, and Numbers records what happened to the man who struck it a second time when he had been told to speak to it instead.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew tsur (H6697), a rock, cliff; olam (H5769), age, everlasting; sela (H5553), a crag, stronghold; Greek petra (G4073), a rock, bedrock.

expand to see more

Hebrew tsur olamim (H6697, H5769) — rock of ages; Isaiah 26:4 margin; tsur also Deuteronomy 32:4, 32:15, Psalm 18:2, 62:2.

Hebrew sela (H5553) — crag, cliff, stronghold; Psalm 18:2, 31:3, 40:2, Exodus 33:22.

Greek petra (G4073) — rock, bedrock; 1 Corinthians 10:4, Matthew 7:24–25, 16:18.

Usage

"“In the LORD JEHOVAH is everlasting strength” — margin: the rock of ages."

"“He is the Rock, his work is perfect” — defined by character, not size."

"“That Rock was Christ” — the supply was a Person."
